walkthroughs.body_html:
Characteristics & Classification — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Characteristics & Classification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Characteristics & Classification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What makes the antigen-binding site of an antibody specific to one antigen?
options: Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
The variable region — its amino acid sequence (and thus shape) differs between antibodies, complementing a specific antigen.
All antibodies have the same binding site; specificity comes from where they go in the body.
Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
A series of chemical reactions in cells that break down glucose to release energy as ATP.
Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Respiration means breathing — inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
